subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: What boundary should OpenClaw enforce for protected config writes that originate from agent-visible errors, host exec, and plugin or cron automation?
rationale: The evidence shows remaining model-visible config hints and a CLI patch path outside the gateway-tool guard, but the reported automatic writer is not identified and the right fix may change security posture, operator workflow, and plugin cron behavior.

options.title: Enforce operator-approved protected writes
options.body: Remove protected config assignments from model-visible error text and require explicit operator provenance, approval, or audit classification before plugin/cron or exec-mediated protected config writes can persist.

options.title: Do text-only hardening first
options.body: Land a narrow copy change for assistant-visible sandbox errors while keeping this issue open for CLI/plugin mutation provenance and audit semantics.

options.title: Allow explicit opt-in automation
options.body: Permit plugin or agent automation to patch protected config only behind a clearly named operator-controlled policy and audit event, accepting a larger config/API decision.

recommendation.title: Enforce operator-approved protected writes
recommendation.body: Remove protected config assignments from model-visible error text and require explicit operator provenance, approval, or audit classification before plugin/cron or exec-mediated protected config writes can persist.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question centers on extending or complementing the protected gateway config-write guard introduced in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts`.
